newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Q1 tax revenues far below budget -state.
newsitem.headline: German Q1 tax revenues far below budget -state.

text.p: Tax revenues lagged far below budget estimates across Germany in the first quarter of 1997, Gerhard Mayer-Vorfelder, finance minister of the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg, said in a statement on Wednesday.
"Tax revenues in the first quarter of 1997 remained far below expectations nationwide," he said, adding that further spending cuts would be needed.
German Q1 tax revenues far below budget -state

For Baden-Wuerttemberg alone, tax revenues in the first quarter were 1.043 billion marks below budget targets, but spending cuts had enabled the state to reduce the gap to about 600 million marks, or 10.7 percent of budgeted levels, he said.
"Further savings measures lie ahead of us," he said. More details from other states will be compiled in Bonn's next tax estimate, due in mid-May.

Germany's efforts to rein in its budget deficit to qualify for the single European currency apply not just to the federal budget but to the total public-sector deficit, including state and local governments.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel projects the 1997 deficit at 2.9 percent of gross domestic product, just below the 3.0 percent threshold, but tax revenue shortfalls are fueling scepticism that Germany can meet the target.
